## Best 2kWh portable power station for an RV under $900

**My top recommendation is the BLUETTI AC200L at $899, or $854.05 with the reported discount code.**

Based on your nine supplied pages, it offers the strongest overall combination of RV compatibility, battery capacity, inverter power, solar charging, and price.

<AsyncImageGroup query={["BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view TT-30 RV outlet","BLUETTI AC200L portable power station RV camping setup"]} aspectRatio="5:4" layout="bento"/>

## Top 5 compared

| Model | Capacity | AC output | RV TT-30 | Weight | Price |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | 2,048 Wh | 2,400 W | Yes | 62.4 lb | **$899** |
| Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO | 2,048 Wh | 2,400 W | Yes | 51 lb | $676.16 |
| OUPES Mega 2 Pro | 2,048 Wh | 2,500 W | Yes | 48.8 lb | $699 |
| Dabbsson DBS2100 Pro | 2,150 Wh | 2,400 W | Yes | 54 lb | $799 |
| ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 | 1,920 Wh | 2,500 W | Yes | 63.9 lb | $650 |

Sources: [DealElectric comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv), [GearRanking RV rankings](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/rv/).

## Why I'd choose the BLUETTI AC200L

<AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station product image" aspectRatio="4:3"/>

- **RV-ready:** Built-in TT-30 30A outlet lets you connect your RV shore-power cord directly.
- **Good power:** 2,400W continuous output handles many everyday RV appliances.
- **Excellent solar charging:** Up to 1,200W solar input, the highest among the compared models in the DealElectric article.
- **LiFePO₄ battery:** A durable chemistry suitable for frequent camping and recharging.
- **Competitive price:** $899, reportedly $854.05 with code `AFF5OFF`.
- **Expandable ecosystem:** Supports additional charging options, including an alternator charger.

**Buy:** [BLUETTI AC200L — deal link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)

Source: [DealElectric's October 31 comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv).

## Best alternatives depending on your priorities

  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **Best budget pick: Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO**

      $676.16 · 2,048Wh · 2,400W · 51 lb

      Saves about $223 versus the BLUETTI, with comparable capacity and output.

      [GearRanking](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/rv/)
    </box>
  </row>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="OUPES Mega 2 Pro portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **Best balance of price and weight: OUPES Mega 2 Pro**

      $699 · 2,048Wh · 2,500W · 48.8 lb

      A good middle ground if you want a lighter unit without sacrificing capacity.

      [GearRanking](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/rv/)
    </box>
  </row>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **Best lightweight option: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2**

      $899.99 · 2kWh class · 41.7 lb

      Worth considering if moving the station in and out of your RV is a priority.

      [DealElectric](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)
    </box>
  </row>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Dabbsson DBS2100 Pro portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **Best extra capacity: Dabbsson DBS2100 Pro**

      $799 · 2,150Wh · 2,400W · 54 lb

      Slightly more battery capacity than the standard 2,048Wh models.

      [GearRanking](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/rv/)
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

## How long will 2kWh last in your RV?

The DealElectric article estimates that approximately **85% of rated capacity is available for AC use**, or roughly 1,700Wh from a 2,048Wh battery.

| RV appliance | Estimated consumption |
|---|---:|
| 12V compressor refrigerator | ~700 Wh/day |
| Furnace blower | 300–500 Wh/night |
| Lights, phones, water pump, fan | ~200 Wh/day |
| **Combined** | **1.2–1.5 kWh/day** |

That translates to roughly **1–1.5 days without recharging**, or potentially 2–3 days with 200–400W of solar under favorable conditions.

Important: A typical RV rooftop air conditioner is not a realistic sustained load for a 2kWh station. Also, the TT-30 outlet does not provide a full 30A of usable power; the 2,400W inverter limits it to approximately 20A.

Source: [DealElectric — RV runtime and charging estimates](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv).

## Bottom line

If I were spending up to $900 for RV boondocking:

- **Best overall:** BLUETTI AC200L at $899 (or the reported $854.05 sale price).
- **Best value:** Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO at $676.16.
- **Best for portability:** Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 at 41.7 lb.

I'd personally lean toward the **BLUETTI AC200L** if solar recharging and direct RV hookup matter most. Prices and promotions can change, so verify the discount in the checkout cart before purchasing.
